AUTHORIZED LIFECYCLE DEPENDENCY DAG CONTRACT v5.
The interpreter starts with an empty resource table, no inheritance edges, and
no checkpoints. The protected resources are the entity names introduced by register_resource.
Their two-digit suffix defines ascending order. Each resource has local
capability, effective capability, authorization revision, and dirty. Directed
weighted inheritance edges only go from a lower suffix to a higher suffix.

The complete mutation semantics follow. register_resource(n,b): set local and
effective capability to b mod 997, revision=0, dirty=false.
add_inheritance(p,c,w): require p<c; insert or replace p->c with weight w mod
997, then mark c and every transitive descendant dirty.
remove_inheritance(p,c): if the edge exists remove it and mark c and every
transitive descendant dirty; otherwise ignore.
rotate_local_capability(n,b): set local capability=b mod 997, increment n's
authorization revision, and mark n plus every transitive descendant dirty.
reconcile_resource(n): apply only when every direct parent is clean. Set
effective capability=(local capability + sum(parent effective capability *
edge weight)) mod 997, set dirty=false, and increment authorization revision.
Otherwise ignore.
reconcile_all(): visit resources in ascending suffix order and reconcile each
dirty resource once its parents are clean. One ascending pass cleans all.
checkpoint_authorization(label,S): save local capability, effective capability,
and dirty for ordered scope S, replacing the label.
restore_authorization(label,S): restore saved local capability, effective
capability, and dirty for resources in both scopes and increment each restored
resource's current authorization revision; then mark every descendant outside
the restored set dirty. Ignore if the intersection is empty.
Every acknowledgement exposes only applied/ignored, never current capability
values. Re-adding an inheritance edge replaces its weight.

audit_authorized_transitions processes requests in their listed order. Before
the first request, a resource lifecycle state is STATES[(effective+revision)
mod 4], where STATES is [provisioned,active,suspended,retired]; lifecycle
version equals authorization revision. Principal p is authorized for resource
suffix s iff (effective + 37*p + 11*s) mod 7 is 0, 1, or 2. A request is
allowed only when, in precedence order: the resource is clean; the principal
is authorized; expected_version equals current version; from_state equals
current state; and to_state is legal under provisioned->active,
active->{suspended,retired}, suspended->{active,retired}, retired->{}. On an
allowed request, set state=to_state and increment version. Denial reasons are
dirty_capability, access_denied, version_mismatch, stale_state, and
illegal_transition in that precedence; reason=allowed for an allowed request.
Output exact compact JSON containing ordered results and final_records. Each
result contains request, resource,
principal, allowed, reason, observed_state, observed_version, and
effective_capability. final_records contains resource, state, version,
effective_capability, and dirty in request-resource first-appearance order.
For structured scoring, order_sensitive=true applies to array element order;
JSON object-key order remains nonsemantic. No unstated defaults exist.

ATOMIC WEIGHTED-QUORUM LIFECYCLE BATCH CONTRACT v1.
audit_quorum_lifecycle_batches is a separate read-only counterfactual audit.
It uses the final capability records produced by the mutation history above,
but replaces the single-principal authorization rule of
audit_authorized_transitions with the exact sponsor quorum below.

The input is ordered batches. Every request contains request, resource,
sponsors, threshold, requires, expected_version, from_state, and to_state.
Sponsors and requires preserve their listed order. Sponsor principal p has
weight 1 + ((effective_capability + 17*p + 13*resource_suffix) mod 5). That
sponsor is an explicit veto exactly when
(effective_capability + 19*p + 7*resource_suffix) mod 11 equals 0. vote_total
is the sum of sponsor weights. A quorum passes iff there is no veto and
vote_total >= threshold.

Batches are processed in listed order. Every request in a batch is preflighted
against the same state at the start of that batch. A requires identifier is
satisfied only when that exact request committed in an earlier batch; requests
inside the current batch cannot satisfy one another. The denial precedence is
dirty_capability, explicit_veto, quorum_shortfall, dependency_uncommitted,
version_mismatch, stale_state, and illegal_transition. Lifecycle states,
initial versions, and legal transitions are exactly those in the contract
above. If every preflight reason is allowed, all transitions commit atomically,
each version increments by one, and every request identifier becomes committed.
If any preflight fails, no transition in the batch commits. Requests whose own
preflight would otherwise be allowed receive reason=batch_aborted; requests
with a specific failing reason retain that reason. All rolled-back requests
have allowed=false. There are no partial commits or unstated retries.

The exact output is {batches,committed_requests,final_records}. Batch rows
preserve input order and contain batch, committed, and ordered results. Every
result contains request, resource, sponsors, sponsor_weights, vote_total,
threshold, requires, allowed, reason, observed_state, observed_version, and
effective_capability. sponsor_weights preserves sponsor order and each row is
{principal,weight,veto}. committed_requests lists successful request identifiers
in commit order. final_records contains resource,state,version,
effective_capability,dirty in resource first-appearance order across all
requests. Array order is semantic and exact; JSON object-key order is
nonsemantic. No hidden defaults exist.

ATOMIC LIFECYCLE TRANSITION FRONTIER PROJECTION v1.
audit_lifecycle_transition_frontier applies the complete ATOMIC
WEIGHTED-QUORUM LIFECYCLE BATCH CONTRACT above, then projects only transition
outcomes. The exact output is {batches,changed_resources,rolled_back_batches,
final_lifecycle}. batches preserves input batch order. Each batch row is
{batch,committed,transitions}; transitions preserves request order and every
row is {request,resource,requested_from,requested_to,observed_state,
observed_version,outcome_state,outcome_version,changed,reason}. When the batch
commits, outcome_state is requested_to, outcome_version is observed_version+1,
changed is true, and reason is allowed. When the batch rolls back,
outcome_state/version equal observed_state/version, changed is false, and
reason is the full audit's specific failure or batch_aborted. changed_resources
lists resource identifiers in first successful transition order, without
duplicates. rolled_back_batches lists failed batch identifiers in input order.
final_lifecycle contains {resource,state,version} in resource first-appearance
order across all requests. Array order is semantic and exact; JSON object-key
order is nonsemantic. No extra capability, vote, or authorization fields are
returned and no hidden defaults exist.

BITEMPORAL EVENT HISTORY CONTRACT v1.
System sequence is the one-based sequence printed in every event acknowledgement. Valid-time intervals are half-open [valid_from,valid_to).
put(id,entity,valid_from,valid_to,value): require a new id and valid_from<valid_to; append that record at the current system sequence. Otherwise ignore.
retract(id): if id names an existing record not previously retracted, mark its retraction at the current system sequence. Otherwise ignore.
At query as_of_system=S, a record is visible exactly when its put sequence is <=S and it has no retraction sequence <=S. A visible record covers valid_time=V exactly when valid_from<=V<valid_to.
resolve(entity,V,S): among visible covering records for entity choose the one with greatest put sequence. Return its id,value,put_sequence,valid_from,valid_to; return status=missing if none.
audit(Q) resolves every labeled query in the requested order and returns compact JSON with records, resolved_count, and resolved_value_sum_mod_997. JSON object-key order is not semantic. Event acknowledgements reveal applied/ignored and system sequence but do not reveal current resolutions. No unstated side effects exist.

put(id,entity,valid_from,valid_to,value): require a new id and valid_from<valid_to; append that record at the current system sequence. Otherwise ignore.
retract(id): if id names an existing record not previously retracted, mark its retraction at the current system sequence. Otherwise ignore.
At query as_of_system=S, a record is visible exactly when its put sequence is <=S and it has no retraction sequence <=S. A visible record covers valid_time=V exactly when valid_from<=V<valid_to.
resolve(entity,V,S): among visible covering records for entity choose the one with greatest put sequence. Return its id,value,put_sequence,valid_from,valid_to; return status=missing if none.
audit(Q) resolves every labeled query in the requested order and returns compact JSON with records, resolved_count, and resolved_value_sum_mod_997. JSON object-key order is not semantic. Event acknowledgements reveal applied/ignored and system sequence but do not reveal current resolutions. No unstated side effects exist.

AUTHORIZED LIFECYCLE DEPENDENCY DAG CONTRACT v5.
The interpreter starts with an empty resource table, no inheritance edges, and
no checkpoints. The protected resources are the entity names introduced by register_resource.
Their two-digit suffix defines ascending order. Each resource has local
capability, effective capability, authorization revision, and dirty. Directed
weighted inheritance edges only go from a lower suffix to a higher suffix.

The complete mutation semantics follow. register_resource(n,b): set local and
effective capability to b mod 997, revision=0, dirty=false.
add_inheritance(p,c,w): require p<c; insert or replace p->c with weight w mod
997, then mark c and every transitive descendant dirty.
remove_inheritance(p,c): if the edge exists remove it and mark c and every
transitive descendant dirty; otherwise ignore.
rotate_local_capability(n,b): set local capability=b mod 997, increment n's
authorization revision, and mark n plus every transitive descendant dirty.
reconcile_resource(n): apply only when every direct parent is clean. Set
effective capability=(local capability + sum(parent effective capability *
edge weight)) mod 997, set dirty=false, and increment authorization revision.
Otherwise ignore.
reconcile_all(): visit resources in ascending suffix order and reconcile each
dirty resource once its parents are clean. One ascending pass cleans all.
checkpoint_authorization(label,S): save local capability, effective capability,
and dirty for ordered scope S, replacing the label.
restore_authorization(label,S): restore saved local capability, effective
capability, and dirty for resources in both scopes and increment each restored
resource's current authorization revision; then mark every descendant outside
the restored set dirty. Ignore if the intersection is empty.
Every acknowledgement exposes only applied/ignored, never current capability
values. Re-adding an inheritance edge replaces its weight.

audit_authorized_transitions processes requests in their listed order. Before
the first request, a resource lifecycle state is STATES[(effective+revision)
mod 4], where STATES is [provisioned,active,suspended,retired]; lifecycle
version equals authorization revision. Principal p is authorized for resource
suffix s iff (effective + 37*p + 11*s) mod 7 is 0, 1, or 2. A request is
allowed only when, in precedence order: the resource is clean; the principal
is authorized; expected_version equals current version; from_state equals
current state; and to_state is legal under provisioned->active,
active->{suspended,retired}, suspended->{active,retired}, retired->{}. On an
allowed request, set state=to_state and increment version. Denial reasons are
dirty_capability, access_denied, version_mismatch, stale_state, and
illegal_transition in that precedence; reason=allowed for an allowed request.
Output exact compact JSON containing ordered results and final_records. Each
result contains request, resource,
principal, allowed, reason, observed_state, observed_version, and
effective_capability. final_records contains resource, state, version,
effective_capability, and dirty in request-resource first-appearance order.
For structured scoring, order_sensitive=true applies to array element order;
JSON object-key order remains nonsemantic. No unstated defaults exist.

DENIAL-PRECEDENCE PROJECTION v1.
audit_authorized_transition_denial_summary processes the ordered requests with
the exact authorization, transition, mutation, and reason-precedence rules
above, but returns only compact JSON containing outcomes, reason_counts,
first_denial_by_reason, allowed_count, and denied_count. outcomes contains
request, resource, allowed, and reason for every request in request order.
reason_counts contains only observed reasons sorted lexically, as reason and
count. first_denial_by_reason contains only observed non-allowed reasons sorted
lexically, as reason and the first request with that reason. allowed_count and
denied_count count outcomes. Array order is semantic; object-key order is not.
